claims.text: Variable-scan-speed selective laser melting can create a fine-grained near-surface layer and a coarse-grained interior in NbMoTaW.
A heat treatment lower in temperature and shorter in duration than 1200°C for 1 hour can relieve internal stresses while preserving the spatial grain-size gradient.
As-built SLM NbMoTaW exhibits microstructural heterogeneity typical of as-built powders.
The proposed processing produces a deliberately maintained fine-surface/coarse-core gradient architecture.
The fine-grained surface reduces stress concentrations.
The fine-grained surface activates multiple deformation pathways.
Reduced stress concentrations and multiple deformation pathways enhance ductility and promote a more uniform strain distribution.
The coarse-grained core retains high strength.
The coarse-grained core enables effective absorption and dissipation of energy during impact.
Impact-energy absorption and dissipation by the coarse-grained core preserve the alloy's impact-induced energy-release properties.
Relative to a uniformly coarse-grained baseline, the gradient-treated alloy will have improved tensile ductility.
Relative to the baseline, the gradient-treated alloy will deform more uniformly during tensile and impact tests.
The gradient-treated alloy's yield strength will be comparable to or only slightly lower than that of the uniformly coarse-grained baseline.
The gradient-treated alloy's impact-induced energy release will be comparable to or only slightly lower than that of the uniformly coarse-grained baseline.
Standard SLM followed by conventional heat treatment produces a homogeneous coarse-grained NbMoTaW baseline.
The predicted benefits should hold at room temperature.
The predicted benefits should hold under dynamic impact loading if the heat treatment preserves the gradient.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis says strength and impact-induced energy release will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome permits both to be slightly lower than the baseline.

The mechanism invokes absorption and dissipation of impact energy as the basis for preserving impact-induced energy release, but energy absorption/dissipation and energetic release are distinct outcomes and their asserted equivalence is not internally explained.
